On Tue, Aug 14, 2028 at 9:12 AM Samantha Lee <samantha@brightpathhealth.com> wrote:
> We started seeing a sharp increase in end-to-end latency for our live chat (SSE)...

Quick tech summary from runtime: we see a concurrent-connection concentration on a small subset of GPU pools (pool-id: gpu-us-west-3a) which pushed memory pressure and caused aggressive KV cache eviction. That leads to more frequent full-token recomputations and higher tail latency for long-running streams.

What we've done (applied at 09:40 PDT):
- Triggered an emergency horizontal scale-up on gpu-us-west-3a (extra dedicated instances added).
- Enabled routing fallback so new connects are routed to the low-latency variant (streaming-variant-v2) with smaller per-request cache window.
- Temporarily decreased per-session batching and increased the token-split threshold to reduce KV working set.

Remaining risk: existing long-lived connections still on the hot nodes will show tail latency until they reconnect or until we drain / recycle instances.

Recommended next step (approved by Eng Ops): perform a rolling drain+recreate of 25% of the affected nodes to avoid mass reconnect storms. This will cause transient disconnects (~20–45s) for sessions on those nodes.

Samantha — quick update from ops:

What we've applied so far (09:40–11:30 PDT):
- Autoscaler fired and spun up +6 nodes in the affected pool; memory/cpu pressure dropped ~30%.
- Fallback routing is active for new connections; traffic split currently ~65% to primary, 35% to fallback.
- Reduced batching and raised token-split as Stephanie outlined.

Observed impact: p95 is back to baseline (~220ms) but p99 for long sessions remains elevated (~1.1–1.6s) likely due to KV thrash on existing connections.

Plan: we propose a rolling drain of 25% of nodes in gpu-us-west-3a starting at 13:00 PDT. Expected outcome: reconnects will move many sessions to the healthier nodes / fallback. Expected user-visible reconnection window ~20–45s for affected sessions.

Jonas / Laura, can you confirm customer approval to proceed? If approved we will execute and monitor; if you want a less disruptive option we can extend fallback routing to 60% but that may increase unit cost and slightly increase median latency for some users.
